source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Social Studies, Grade 5 (First Published 2017, Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly from 'grade 5 designs/GRADE-5-SOCIAL-STUDIES-Curriculum-Designs.pdf' via the Read tool (no pages param), full text extracted. 5 strands / 22 sub-strands / 90 lessons total. Social Studies is an integrated study of Social Sciences and Humanities (History, Geography, Citizenship Education, Sociology, plus selected Agriculture/Science/Psychology concepts) per its own essence statement.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Elements of a Map
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key elements of a map
Illustrate key elements of a map on a sketch
Interpret features in a map using key elements
Appreciate the use of maps in daily life
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we use maps in our daily lives?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm in groups the key elements of a map
Locate elements of a map using a sketch map, wall map, atlas or digital maps
Draw a sketch map and label the key elements
Practise reading and interpreting a map using the key elements
Play computer games in groups on the elements of a map (digital, atlas, wall maps)
Discuss the various areas where maps are used in daily lives

subStrands.name: 1.2 Location, Position and Size of Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify countries that neighbour Kenya
Locate the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours using a compass direction
Value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours?
learningExperiences: Draw a map of Kenya and indicate her neighbours
Use an atlas/appropriate media to identify the position of Kenya relative to her neighbours
Discuss the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours
Play games, in pairs, on locating places on a map
Find out the size of Kenya using digital resources and share in class
Draw a map of Kenya and indicate the size in square kilometres
Compose songs and poems about Kenya and her neighbours
scopeNotes: Kenya's neighbouring countries (per compass direction context): Ethiopia, Somalia, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan (5 countries), reachable from atlas/digital-map tasks the design specifies without naming them verbatim — treat as standard, well-known geography content consistent with this sub-strand's scope.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Main Physical Features in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify main physical features in Kenya
Show main physical features in Kenya on a map
Value physical features found in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are physical features useful in a country?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm and identify physical features found in Kenya
Use digital and print resources to locate the main physical features in Kenya
Locate the main physical features using a sketch map or atlas
Draw a map of Kenya and locate the main physical features
Collect and display maps and pictures showing the main physical features in Kenya
Care for the physical features found in the immediate environment

subStrands.name: 1.4 Weather and Climate
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify elements of weather in the environment
Show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map
Describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya
Acknowledge different weather and climatic conditions in planning for day-to-day activities
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we experience different climatic conditions in Kenya?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm in groups the difference between weather and climate
Discuss in groups elements of weather (rainfall, wind, temperature, cloud cover)
Use digital maps/atlas to locate the main climatic regions of Kenya
Discuss the characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya
Model in groups a map of Kenya showing the main climatic regions and display in class
Find out from parents/guardians the effects of extreme weather conditions

subStrands.name: 1.5 The Built Environments
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify main historic built environments in Kenya
Show main historic built environments in Kenya on a map
Apply strategies to conserve historic built environments for preservation of cultural heritage
Appreciate the need for conserving historic built environments in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we conserve the historic built environments?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the main historic built environments in Kenya
Use digital/print resources to identify historic built environments
Use a map of Kenya to locate some historic built environments
Develop posters/charts/flip cards with messages on the importance of caring for historic built environments
Visit/virtual visit a nearby historic built environment/library/cultural centre and share experiences
Seek advice from a resource person on ways of conserving historic built environments
Participate in conservation activities for historic built environments in the locality

subStrands.name: 2.1 Language Groups in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify main language groups in Kenya
Explain benefits of interdependence of language groups in Kenya
Show the interdependence of language groups in Kenya
Appreciate the interdependence of language groups
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we benefit by interacting with different language groups in Kenya?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the main language groups in Kenya
Discuss ways in which different language groups depend on each other in Kenya
Engage a resource person to find out the benefits of interdependence of language groups
Role-play scenarios that depict interdependence of language groups in Kenya
Compose poems and songs that depict interdependence during cultural events
Narrate African stories on the origin of various language groups in Kenya

subStrands.name: 2.2 Population Distribution in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the effects of population density in different regions in Kenya
Show areas of high and low population density in Kenya on a map
Acknowledge the impact of population distribution in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: How is population distribution useful in Kenya?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm areas of high and low population density in Kenya
Use digital or print resources to locate areas of high and low population density
Shade areas of low and high population density on a sketch map of Kenya
Create a skit that depicts the impact of population distribution in Kenya

subStrands.name: 2.3 African Traditional Education
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify methods of instruction used in African traditional education
Explain the importance of African traditional education in promoting values
Apply African traditional education in promoting values
Appreciate the role of African traditional education in promoting values
keyInquiryQuestions: How does African traditional education promote values in our community?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the meaning of African traditional education
Discuss methods of instruction used in African traditional education such as narratives, stories, songs, riddles and proverbs
Watch video tapes/listen to narratives, stories/observe pictures on aspects of African traditional education
Engage with a resource person on methods of instruction used in African traditional education
Discuss the importance of African traditional education in promoting values
Design posters on methods of instruction used in African traditional education
Find out from parents/guardians the methods of instruction used and share in class

subStrands.name: 2.4 School Administration
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify administrative leaders in a school
State duties of administrative leaders in a school
Illustrate administrative structure of a school
Appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school
keyInquiryQuestions: How is school administration organised?
learningExperiences: Discuss the administrative leaders in school
Discuss the order of administration in school
Use digital or print resources to search duties of administrative leaders in school
Share with parents or guardians the duties of school administrators
Draw and display in class the administrative structure of the school

subStrands.name: 3.1 Resources in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify resources found in Kenya
Explain the benefits of using available resources prudently
Illustrate ways in which available resources can be used sustainably
Appreciate the resources available in society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to use resources prudently?
How can we conserve resources in our society?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm on resources found in Kenya
Take a nature walk around the school locality to collect samples of resources found
State the benefits of using available resources prudently
Engage a resource person to find out the benefits of using available resources prudently
Search online or use print media on ways in which available resources can be used sustainably
Write articles/sensitisation messages on prudent use of resources found in Kenya

subStrands.name: 3.2 Mining in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify major minerals found in Kenya
Use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals
Examine the importance of minerals in Kenya
Acknowledge the contribution of mining to the economy of Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we benefit from the minerals found in our country?
How does the government promote mining in Kenya?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm on minerals found in Kenya
Use digital or print resources to identify minerals found in Kenya
Draw a map of Kenya and locate major minerals
Engage with a resource person to discuss the importance of minerals in society
Create posters on contribution of mining to the economy of Kenya
Visit a mining site/quarry or watch a documentary on the importance of mining and write a report

subStrands.name: 3.3 Fishing in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify main inland fishing grounds in Kenya
Locate main inland fishing grounds in Kenya
Explain contribution of fishing to the economy of Kenya
Recognise fishing as an economic activity
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is fishing important in our country?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm on the main inland fishing grounds in Kenya
Draw a map of Kenya showing the main inland fishing grounds
Find out the contribution of fishing to the economy of Kenya and write a summary
Engage with a resource person to discuss the contribution of fishing to the economy
Develop posters on the importance of fishing in Kenya
Illustrate fishing methods used in Kenya, display in class, gallery walk

subStrands.name: 3.4 Wildlife and Tourism in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify main tourist attractions in Kenya
Locate main game reserves and national parks in Kenya
Explain contributions of wildlife and tourism to the economy
Acknowledge the contribution of wildlife and tourism to the economy of Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is wildlife important?
learningExperiences: Discuss who is a tourist
Use digital or print resources to identify tourist attractions in Kenya
Brainstorm the difference between a game reserve and a national park
Draw a map of Kenya and show the main game reserves and national parks (named above)
Discuss the contributions of wildlife and tourism to the economy and present in class
Debate on the contribution of tourism to the economy of Kenya
Write an essay on the contribution of tourism to the economy of Kenya

subStrands.name: 3.5 Development of Transport
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline main means of early transport to facilitate movement of goods and services
Identify modern means of transport in Kenya
Explore ways of maintaining road safety in society
Apply safety precautions in using means of transport
Appreciate the role of modern means of transport in national development
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is transport important in development?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the meaning of transport
Find out the main early means of transport (human porterage, pack animals, logging/log and boats, rafts) and share
Sketch the early means of transport and present in class
Identify modern means of transport in Kenya
Draw the road signs in Kenya and display them in class
Role-play safe practices of a pedestrian crossing (walking not running, walk on a line/single file)
Find out ways of observing road safety and write a report
Role-play how to observe traffic rules while using the road

subStrands.name: 3.6 Development of Communication
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline main early forms of communication to facilitate social interactions
Explore modern means of communication in Kenya
Illustrate modern means of communication used in their community
Recognise the role of modern means of communication in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is communication important?
learningExperiences: Find out the main early forms of communication and share in class
Sketch the early forms of communication and present in class
Discuss modern means of communication in Kenya
Draw different modern means of communication and display in class
Role-play use of various modern means of communication

subStrands.name: 4.1 Traditional Leaders in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline leadership qualities of selected traditional leaders in Kenya
Illustrate contributions of selected traditional leaders in Kenya
Recognise the role of traditional leaders in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are traditional leaders important in the community?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm leadership qualities of the selected traditional leaders
Observe pictures of selected traditional leaders using appropriate media
Gather information and do a write-up on the contributions of selected traditional leaders
Illustrate contributions using charts and display in class
Collect and creatively display portraits/pictures of the selected traditional leaders
Draw, colour and display pictures of selected traditional leaders
scopeNotes: Kivoi wa Mwendwa: 19th-century Akamba (Kamba) trader/leader known for long-distance trade routes. Mekatilili wa Menza: early-20th-century Giriama (Mijikenda) leader who led resistance against British colonial rule. Only these 2 leaders are named in the design — a closed, small list.

subStrands.name: 4.2 Early Forms of Government in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe early forms of government among selected communities in Kenya
Compare early forms of government of the Maasai and Ameru
Apply best practices from early forms of government among selected communities to modern governance
Appreciate the importance of early forms of governance in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: How were communities ruled in the past?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm forms of government in their community
Describe early forms of government (e.g. Maasai age-set/council-of-elders system; Ameru Njuri Ncheke council of elders)
Find out from the library the early forms of government among the Maasai and Ameru
Develop a chart illustrating differences and similarities between Maasai and Ameru early government
Create a simple journal on best practices from these early forms of government
Role-play early forms of government among the Maasai or the Ameru
scopeNotes: Design names exactly 2 communities (Maasai, Ameru) for comparison — a closed pair, not an open list.

subStrands.name: 4.3 Citizenship in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: State how one becomes a citizen in Kenya
Explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya
Demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being
Appreciate being a good citizen in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote responsible citizenship?
learningExperiences: Discuss ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen (birth, registration, naturalisation)
Find out ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen and share in class
Debate on dual citizenship in Kenya
Develop communication messages on good citizenship
Write an essay on what may happen if one lost Kenyan citizenship
Create and recite poems on Kenyan citizenship
Develop intergroup communication skills for peaceful coexistence

subStrands.name: 5.1 National Unity in Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify national symbols in Kenya
Explain factors which promote national unity in Kenya
Illustrate ways of overcoming challenges of national unity
Develop national awareness to enhance social cohesion among diverse communities
Embrace a sense of nationhood and patriotism for harmonious living
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote national unity in our country?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm on national symbols in Kenya (coat of arms, national flag, national anthem, public seal)
Identify the national symbols using appropriate media
Draw and colour the national symbols using locally available materials
Brainstorm factors which promote national unity
Engage a resource person on ways of overcoming challenges of national unity
Role-play national awareness to enhance social cohesion among diverse communities
Write down and sing the three stanzas of the National Anthem of Kenya
Find out about national days in Kenya from parents/guardians/elders and write a report

subStrands.name: 5.2 Human Rights
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify basic human rights in Kenya
Explain the importance of human rights in society
Create awareness on the importance of respecting human rights in society
Apply ways to protect human rights in society
Appreciate the importance of respecting human rights in society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to respect human rights?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm on the meaning of human rights
Identify the basic human rights in Kenya using appropriate media
Discuss the importance of human rights in society and present in class
Develop posters to create awareness on the importance of respecting human rights
Act a skit on how to apply ways of protecting human rights
Engage with a resource person on the importance of human rights and write a report
Recite poems and sing songs on the importance of human rights

subStrands.name: 5.3 Democracy in Society
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify types of democracy in Kenya
Explain benefits of democracy in society
Practise democracy in governance in the community
Desire to promote democracy in society
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we practise democracy in our society?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the meaning of democracy
Find out types of democracy in Kenya (direct, indirect) and write short notes
Discuss and list the benefits of democracy in society
Engage with a resource person to discuss the benefits of democracy
Develop posters on benefits of democracy, display in class and share
Recite poems/sing songs on the importance of democracy

subStrands.name: 5.4 National Government
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya
Illustrate the three arms of National Government in Kenya
Desire to participate in national governance in the country
keyInquiryQuestions: How does the government work?
learningExperiences: Brainstorm the three arms of National Government in Kenya and share in class
Discuss the three arms of National Government using appropriate media and list them down
Find out the three arms of National Government using relevant sources
Illustrate the three arms of the National Government and display them in class
